quarterly_data.signal: CFO fiscal Q4 2026 guide beyond revenue / EPS: AGS revenue of about $1.84 billion (up 22% YoY); other revenue of around $510 million, composed primarily of display revenue; non-GAAP gross margin approximately 50.4% (up 230 basis points YoY); non-GAAP operating expenses around $1.58 billion; non-GAAP tax rate around 11%, and around 13% in 2027 as the company absorbs the global minimum tax. For modelling, other revenue is now expected at approximately $400 million per quarter on average through 2027. Fiscal Q1 2027 is a 14-week quarter with a higher-than-average opex step-up; CFO: 'we do expect sequential growth, in our Q1, the calendar Q4, but not guiding that at this point.' CFO: 'we expect another strong record year in 2027'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 AGS ~$1.84 billion; non-GAAP GM ~50.4%; opex ~$1.58 billion; other revenue ~$510 million

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q3 records by business unit: deposition (PVD, CVD and epitaxy, 'one of our fastest-growing businesses this year'), thermals and treatments in materials modification, etch and CMP in materials removal, and process diagnostics and control, which is growing faster than the overall systems business this year. Semiconductor Systems non-GAAP operating profit rose 45% YoY to a record $2.7 billion. AGS record revenue reflected both subscription services growth and high transactional parts demand; AGS gross margin was 35.6% (up 180 basis points YoY) and operating margin 30.1% (up 280 basis points), which the CFO tied to AGS using AI and warehouse automation to grow as efficiently as possible. OpEx as a percentage of revenue was the lowest in nearly four years. Other revenue was $294 million; capital expenditures $707 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Semi Systems non-GAAP operating profit $2.7 billion (+45% YoY); AGS operating margin 30.1%

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing and margins: CFO said a systematic value-based pricing approach implemented three years ago (every tool repriced) has lifted gross margins to over 50% for the company and over 55% in semiconductor systems - approximately 300 basis points at company level over the last three years - with 'higher pricing and margins in both new and existing products', and 'we are confident we will continue to expand gross margins.' Near term, the guided quarter carries a 'flattish margin at the company level' on ramp costs (customer service engineers and other resources); CFO: 'slow improvement is the right way to think about it', with the headwind receding as revenues grow. AGS: CFO expects to improve services gross margins over time (AIx-based solutions, growing installed base, higher utilization lifting spares); CEO: 'I am more positive on growth in the AGS business, both top line and bottom line, than I've ever been.'
quarterly_data.figure: GM over 50% company, over 55% semi systems; ~300 basis points in three years

quarterly_data.signal: Demand and visibility: CFO said cloud service providers continue to increase AI infrastructure investments and many are already generating positive returns; utilization is rising across the board, including ICAPS, with strong demand in AI-related markets like power and optical chips. For the largest customers Applied has 'probably five years of visibility' to the roadmap and detailed eight-quarter forecasts shared with suppliers; CEO: technology discussions 'go out maybe 10 years in the future'. CFO on the plan to double quarterly system output capacity by 2028: 'it is not a revenue forecast for 2028', but an indication of what Applied will be prepared for. Manufacturing space has nearly doubled over the past several years. CFO on capex: 'it will still be a CapEx year that's higher than normal, but it will decline as a percentage of revenue as we go into 2027.'
quarterly_data.figure: about five years of roadmap visibility; eight-quarter forecasts

quarterly_data.signal: Output innovation and EPIC: CEO said Applied has multiple output innovation products (more wafers processed per square foot of clean room space) in qualification at customer sites that will provide significant increases in output per unit area. EPIC Center in Silicon Valley: 'We will move the first R&D tool into the clean room next week, and we are on track to start operations in the coming months.'

Advanced packaging R&D: CFO said Applied has significantly increased R&D in advanced packaging innovations, supplementing it with two small acquisitions. CEO on hybrid bonding: 'Applied has strong technology in hybrid bonding', with a very big business in the adjacent steps and 'the only integrated R&D facility working with our customers to enable those new architectures for packaging'; CEO expects 'very strong growth in 2027 and going forward' in packaging.
